findings.description: The judgment halves of two blocker clauses are still routed to a deterministic checker, and that dispatch is now the job's next move. T-003's checker is checker-deterministic (haiku, 'they only run scripts' per the routing table), and its check_method assigns it three rubric judgments the constitution declares checker-judgment: B-2 requirement 4 ('read the output of the four all items succeed cases and FAIL on any failure summary, heading, or zero-count'), B-5's output half ('FAIL on an empty or headerless failure summary'), and D-4's stub bullet ('shows a recording stub on PATH for every case executing the raycast script'). This was raised as a major at r1 while T-003 was pending; it is a blocker now because T-003 is assigned with its worker mid-flight, so the wrong-family checker runs next, and when its verdict lands and T-003 goes complete, B-2 requirement 4 and B-5's output half are consumed and no later task re-checks them. That is the same orphaning pattern that failed r0 and r1, completing itself through an assignment rather than an omission: the check exists on paper, is executed by a family the constitution says cannot perform it, and the clause is then closed. The fix is the one the orchestrator already applied twice this round: both bullets move to T-005, whose checker is checker-judgment and whose deps already include T-003, or to T-006. The routing rule is directional, so opus running a grep is fine and haiku rendering a rubric is not.

T-003.md:30 'status: assigned'; dispatches.log:21 '2026-08-07T14:09:15 | agent-guild:worker-standard | T-003 | sonnet' is the last worker dispatch, so T-003's checker is the next move.

findings.description: Unrepaired from r1 and materially worse, because this round's blocker-1 repair added to it. T-005 now carries two blocker clauses whose subject is other tasks' artifacts: V-2 (the whole-suite run over tests/apps.bats, tests/doctor.bats and tests/install-failures.bats, authored by T-001, T-004 and T-003) and D-1 (scope over the four converted scripts and all of tests/). T-005's own worker is a worker-craft scoped by its prose to two files: 'Touch only _working-memory/conventions.md and _working-memory/decisionLog.md.' So a V-2 or D-1 FAIL on T-005 is, on the balance of probability, a FAIL of somebody else's work, and the retry ladder as written re-dispatches the same executor — a prose worker who must either fix bash and bats files or obey its own scope instruction, and cannot do both. The same shape holds for B-2 requirement 4 and B-5's output half on T-003 (the defect they detect lives in T-002's scripts) and for D-4's judgment and repo-state halves on T-006 (the tests/ stubs are T-003's artifact; a boltdb mtime move would be T-002's or T-003's worker). No task file says what a checker or the orchestrator should do with such a FAIL. The r1 remedy still applies unchanged: one sentence per deferral site naming the owning task, so the diagnosis routes there rather than reworking the task that happens to host the check.

findings.description: New this round. T-003's check_method instructs its checker to execute tests/install-failures.bats before verifying that the file stubs `defaults`, which makes the checker itself the agent that can perform D-4's own failing example. The method opens 'B-3 FIRST, because nothing else in this job runs the file against the converted scripts: bats tests/install-failures.bats must pass at HEAD, all 15 cases ok' and places the D-4 stub grep last, five sub-checks later. The rendered configure-raycast script runs `defaults write com.raycast.macos raycastGlobalHotkey`, which ignores $HOME and lands in the real ~/Library/Preferences. If the stub is missing, the first sub-check rewrites the user's global hotkey and only the last sub-check would have caught it. I re-derived that the hazard is not live today — the delivered file defines stub_defaults at tests/install-failures.bats:49-57, recording to DEFAULTS_LOG, and calls it in all four configure-raycast cases — but the ordering is exactly wrong for the moment it matters, which is a rework where the stub regressed. The D-4 stub grep must run before any execution of the file, on every dispatch. The same precedence question applies to T-005's V-2 suite run, which is safe only because T-005 deps on T-003.
findings.evidence: T-003.md:10-11 'B-3 FIRST ... bats tests/install-failures.bats must pass at HEAD' vs T-003.md:23-29 (D-4 stub grep, last). constitution.md:264 'runs `defaults write com.raycast.macos`, which ignores `$HOME` and lands in the real `~/Library/Preferences` — verified'; constitution.md:278 failing example 'a new test executes the rendered raycast script without stubbing `defaults`, silently rewriting the user's global hotkey'. Measured: tests/install-failures.bats:49 `stub_defaults()`, :52 heredoc stub, :57 chmod, called at :178, :186, :209, :230 against the four configure-raycast cases at :176, :184, :207, :228.

findings.description: The skip-line guard's repair swapped one vacuity for a narrower one, and the narrower one has a chained consequence. T-005 replaces the commit-range form with `git diff -- tests/` adds no line matching '^\+[[:space:]]*skip\b'. Measured, that command reports only tests/apps.bats and tests/doctor.bats and yields zero lines for tests/install-failures.bats, because git diff does not show untracked files at all. It also shows worktree-versus-index only, so any worker that `git add`s its work blanks it entirely (nothing is staged right now, so this half is latent rather than live). For V-2's own text — 'No existing case is deleted or skipped to reach green' — the uncommitted form is the right instrument and covers the two modified pre-existing files, so this is not a repair failure. The gap is that the committed-range form, which would have covered the new file's added lines, is now run nowhere: T-006 carries no skip grep. The consequence chains. Measured: bats reports a skipped case as 'ok N title # skip reason' and exits 0. Ten of V-1's fifteen cases are expected to pass at baseline (three absent-tool, three keeps-going, four all-items-succeed), so all ten could carry `skip` and still satisfy T-003's 'all 15 cases ok', V-1's title grep, V-1's `status" -eq 0` count, and V-1's baseline TAP comparison. Skipping the four all-items-succeed cases would additionally make B-2 requirement 4 and B-5's output half vacuous, since neither would have output to read. Not exploited today: `grep -nE '^[[:space:]]*skip\b' tests/install-failures.bats` returns nothing. Fixes: `git diff HEAD -- tests/` closes the staging half, and a direct grep of tests/install-failures.bats closes the untracked half.
findings.evidence: T-005.md:26-27. Measured: `git diff --name-only -- tests/` -> tests/apps.bats, tests/doctor.bats only; `git diff -- tests/ | grep -c install-failures` -> 0; `git status --porcelain -uall` shows '?? tests/install-failures.bats' and ' M' (unstaged) on everything else. Measured bats TAP for a skipped case: 'ok 2 b: skipped # skip because', bats exit 0. constitution.md:196, :200; T-003.md:11, :91-99 (baseline table, 10 expected-pass rows).

findings.description: Carried from r1, unrepaired, and now load-bearing for the blocker-1 repair. T-005's deps are [T-002, T-003]. V-2 was moved onto T-005 on the stated grounds that it is 'the last task before the commit' and so the only place the suite runs 'with the new coverage in place' — but T-004 authors tests/doctor.bats's new case and T-001 authors the tests/apps.bats fix, and neither is in T-005's deps. The ordering holds today only by accident of both being complete with their artifacts in the working tree; nothing in the DAG prevents a T-004 rework landing after T-005's suite run and leaving that green stale, and D-1's working-tree scan has the same exposure. Adding T-001 and T-004 to T-005's deps encodes what the repair's own rationale already assumes.

findings.description: Carried from r1, unrepaired. T-006's check_method still omits D-3's blocked-not-failed rule: 'A commit whose message begins `[auto-sync from` is not a worker's and means the LaunchAgent ran despite the precondition: report `blocked`, not a worker failure.' T-006's prose tells the worker to stop and report it, but the checker's instructions do not, so a checker meeting a machine-authored commit records a worker FAIL and burns a retry against a defect no worker committed. Commit af8fe49 is this having already happened once in this repo.

findings.description: Carried from r0 and r1, unrepaired, and now partly overtaken by events. T-003's check_method still requires 'every required title appears' without writing the fifteen strings out; both T-003 and V-1 give a pattern plus a table whose script prefixes are shortened from the filenames, leaving a haiku checker to derive fifteen exact strings — the step that produces a near-miss grep reported as clean. The risk did not materialize this round: I listed the delivered titles and all fifteen match the derived form exactly. But the checker has not run yet, and a checker that derives its reference strings from the artifact it is checking is validating the file against itself. Fifteen literal strings in T-003 still cost nothing.

findings.description: The apply detector's reference point is a file the orchestrator edits on every status change, so its discriminating power slides forward through the job. T-006 restates the clause as 'chezmoistate.boltdb mtime no later than the job's first task file', which is ambiguous between the lowest-numbered task file and the earliest-mtime one, and either way names a mutable target. Measured: the earliest task-file mtime is 2026-08-07T13:52:40Z (T-001.md, T-004.md), while the job's first worker dispatch was 2026-08-06T22:35:06Z — about fifteen hours of the job sits before the anchor and an apply in that window would read as clean. Sound in fact today, because the boltdb's mtime is 2026-08-06T20:26:14Z, earlier than every task file and earlier than the first dispatch, which is positive evidence no apply has run. A fixed timestamp in the clause or the task, rather than a file whose mtime the orchestrator moves, would keep it that way.
findings.evidence: T-006.md:24-25; constitution.md:270. Measured: stat chezmoistate.boltdb -> 2026-08-06T20:26:14Z; earliest task-file mtime 2026-08-07T13:52:40Z; dispatches.log:8 first worker dispatch 2026-08-06T22:35:06Z.

Blocker 1: V-2 now sits on T-005 alongside D-1 and D-2, and T-005's deps put it after T-002 and T-003 while T-001 and T-004 are already complete with their artifacts in the tree, so `timeout 300 bats tests/` will run with all three new/modified test files present — AC8 is verified for the first time in this decomposition. The per-file @test floors are all six now, closing the r1 major where five of six were checked nowhere, and I re-derived every floor against the baseline. Blocker 2: T-006 carries D-4's judgment half verbatim with a checker-judgment; I diffed its command list against the clause and all eight strings are present in order. T-003's inert `defaults read` probe is gone, replaced by 'The proof is that the stub recorded an invocation, not that the value survived', which is what the clause asks for. T-006's `git status --porcelain` now carries both qualifiers, so it no longer FAILs T-006 for obeying its own instruction to leave the encrypted settings file alone.
